units.source_text: 她们房间的大五屉柜涂上黑漆，雕刻了梧桐花与叶形的家徽；

en.t: The large five-drawer chest in their room was coated in black lacquer and carved with a family crest of paulownia flowers and leaves;

units.source_text: 像铁壶把的手环，早已生了红锈。

en.t: its ring-shaped handles, like the handle of an iron kettle, had long since grown red with rust.

units.source_text: 这些昔日农家的家具，现在用来放换洗的衣物，还放客人的浴衣和床单。

en.t: These pieces of furniture from old farmhouses were now used to store changes of clothing, as well as guests' yukata and bedsheets.

units.source_text: 十叠宽的房间里，每个角落都堆放着一摞摞客用被褥和坐垫。

en.t: In the ten-mat room, every corner was piled high with stacks of bedding and cushions for guests.

units.source_text: 她们的包袱则同布头和空箱一起，凌乱地放在壁橱里。

en.t: Their bundles, together with scraps of cloth and empty boxes, were tossed messily into the closet.

units.source_text: 破旧的化妆台、空肥皂盒做的梳妆盒、旧三弦琴、破洋伞等都放在五屉柜上，或放在墙壁的搁板上。

en.t: A shabby dressing table, a vanity box made from an empty soap box, an old shamisen, a broken Western umbrella, and other things were set on top of the five-drawer chest or on shelves along the wall.

units.source_text: 到处都摆得满满的，也没有主儿。

en.t: Everything everywhere was packed full, and none of it seemed to belong to anyone.

units.source_text: 开始缝制冬天的棉袍了，只见撒满线头和糖纸的旧榻榻米上，剪子闪闪发光。

en.t: They had begun sewing padded winter robes, and on the old tatami strewn with thread ends and candy wrappers, the scissors alone gleamed brightly.
